newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters to set up talks with National, Labour.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters to set up talks with National, Labour.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters on Tuesday said he would contact both the National and Labour parties to set up negotiations following Saturday's general election.

Peters also said he had written to both Prime Minister Jim Bolger and Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash requesting briefings from the Reserve Bank and Treasury. NZ First, which holds the balance of power, is sending its own briefing paper to the National, Labour and Alliance parties.
NZ First's negotiating team is Peters, deputy Tau Henare and MPs Peter McCardle, Doug Woolerton and Wayne Peters.
Asked if the issue of Prime Minister Jim Bolger's leadership was on the talks agenda, Peters told a news conference: "That is not for us to say."
Peters said New Zealand First had said before the election that personalities would not be allowed to get in the way of coalition discussions.

He said the NZ First parliamentary caucus aimed to arrive at a consensus "where we all agree" on a preferred coalition option. "I think we can proceed with confidence that at the end of the day we can come to a united view," he said.
Peters said that he would not give any prgress reports during the discussions. "To expedite it, it needs to be private."
Peters pleaded for patience and calmness from the financial markets.
Both National, the largest party in parliament, and Labour have said they aim to form a government with support from nationalist New Zealand First.
